- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33–0.67 oscillation, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth 30d forecast by 1–2% downward for next 10 days.
